I've re-thought about what to do about incorrect LOCATION headers, and dual stacked devices, and the solution I've come up with is... do nothing! In detail:

Starting with unknown device:
1. Receive search/advertisement message for new UDN on any of the listening sockets
2. Try to retrieve description from device at URL in the LOCATION header. Don't second-guess if it's correct, just try it and see. Let HA's host OS figure out routing and the like.
3. If successful, great! Add the device to the set of known devices. Make sure to record the BOOTID.UPNP.ORG header value.
4. If unsuccessful, ignore error and do nothing else. Don't add device to set of known devices.

Starting with known device (already got description):
1. Receive search/advertisement message for existing UDN (on any of the listening sockets).
2. If BOOTID.UPNP.ORG header value is the same, ignore the message and do nothing. Stop here.
3. If BOOTID.UPNP.ORG header value is different (doesn't matter if greater or lesser, only not-equal matters), then try to retrieve description from device at URL in LOCATION header.
4. If successful, update the details for the device in the set of known devices.
5. If unsuccessful, ignore error and do nothing else.

If get an "ssdp:update" advertisement for a known device, change the recorded BOOTID.UPNP.ORG value and do nothing else. This is only used to prevent re-initialising the device when the next "ssdp:alive" message comes through with a changed BOOTID.

Ok, the problem is that to bind a IPv6 multicast socket (used for SSDP), a so called 'scope_id' is needed. This scope_id is available in home assistant, see https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/6e7fe13d51b7a00791fa054b69eb0f60bd3cca48/homeassistant/components/network/__init__.py#L56

But in Python3.8 the [IPv6Address](https://docs.python.org/3.8/library/ipaddress.html#ipaddress.IPv6Address) does not provide a means to store the scope_id, while [IPv6Address](https://docs.python.org/3.9/library/ipaddress.html#ipaddress.IPv6Address) in Python3.9 does provide it. There is even a [comment in the home assistant source](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/6e7fe13d51b7a00791fa054b69eb0f60bd3cca48/homeassistant/components/network/__init__.py#L55) stating how to use it! :)
